1	---
2	title: Graphics with an agent
3	description: Let an agent write a graphic module, look at its frames, place it on the timeline and check the result, and see what undo covers.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An agent can make a motion graphic from start to finish: read the API, write the module, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.
10	
11	Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
15	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
16	  tools={[
17	    'graphic_reference',
18	    'write_graphic',
19	    'render_graphic',
20	    'get_graphic',
21	    'list_graphics',
22	    'insert_graphic',
23	    'add_graphic_clip',
24	    'set_graphic',
25	    'import_graphic_font',
26	    'import_graphic_asset',
27	    'add_action',
28	    'set_action_end',
29	    'render_frame',
30	  ]}
31	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab with your Anthropic key."
32	/>
33	
34	## The loop
35	
36	<Steps>
37	
38	1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` answers it once, for the whole session.
39	
40	2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` compiles what it wrote and says whether it worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.
41	
42	3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.
43	
44	4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The font's answer gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the picture's gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
45	
46	5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
47	
48	6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.
49	
50	</Steps>
51	
52	## Read the API
53	
54	`graphic_reference` answers the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.
55	
56	No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.
57	
58	## Write a module
59	
60	`write_graphic` writes `graphics/<name>.js` in the project and answers the compile of that exact text. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and a reader never sees half a file.
61	
62	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.
63	
64	The answer says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still an answer, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as calling `asset()` outside `render`.
65	
66	Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).
67	
68	[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.
69	
70	## A contact sheet
71	
72	`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.
73	
74	| Choice | What it does | Default |
75	| --- | --- | --- |
76	| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
77	| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
78	| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
79	| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
80	| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
81	| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |
82	
83	The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.
84	
85	Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.
86	
87	A frame that fails is drawn as its error card, and the answer adds a sentence saying where in the module it failed. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.
88	
89	A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call is refused before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.
90	
91	:::note
92	The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
93	:::
94	
95	## One frame's SVG
96	
97	Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` answers one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.
98	
99	It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is refused. If the frame fails, the answer says so and holds no SVG.
100	
101	## List and insert
102	
103	`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.
104	
105	Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".
106	
107	`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.
108	
109	- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The answer names the module the clip is drawn by.
110	- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
111	- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call is refused with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.
112	
113	See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
114	
115	## Place a clip
116	
117	`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also aim at a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.
118	
119	| Choice | Default | Limit |
120	| --- | --- | --- |
121	| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
122	| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
123	| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |
124	
125	Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed is refused by its name. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.
126	
127	Frame Job won't place the clip when:
128	
129	- The module isn't in the folder. The refusal says what the folder holds.
130	- The module doesn't compile. The refusal gives its first error.
131	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The refusal names the key.
132	- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The refusal names the canvas.
133	
134	## Change a clip
135	
136	`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).
137	
138	- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
139	- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
140	- **In** can't be set. The trims and splits own it.
141	
142	These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.
143	
144	Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.
145	
146	## Read a module or the folder
147	
148	`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. This is what the **Source** section shows a person.
149	
150	With no name it reads the folder:
151	
152	- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
153	- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
154	- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
155	- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
156	- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.
157	
158	## File tools
159	
160	An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.
161	
162	| What | Where |
163	| --- | --- |
164	| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
165	| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
166	| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |
167	
168	`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.
169	
170	In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.
171	
172	See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.
173	
174	## Undo rules
175	
176	The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.
177	
178	| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
179	| --- | --- | --- |
180	| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
181	| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
182	| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
183	| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |
184	
185	Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again. `import_graphic` can't be undone either, and `export_graphic` edits nothing, so it has no undo step.
186	
187	Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts each module replaced, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's text is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
188	
189	## Graphics in render frame
190	
191	`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the answer has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
192	
193	## The Assistant
194	
195	The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).
196	
197	It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.
198	
199	## Related
200	
201	- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
202	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
203	- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
204	- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
205	- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)
206

1	---
2	title: Write a graphic module
3	description: Write your own motion graphic as one JavaScript file, with its name, its properties, the SVG it draws for each frame and the limits it runs under.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A graphic is one JavaScript file whose `render` function returns an SVG picture for each frame. Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
13	  where={['graphics/API.md and graphics/API.d.ts in your project', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source']}
14	  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'render_graphic']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Try your first module
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.
22	
23	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.
24	
25	3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a legal name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.
30	
31	## The module
32	
33	A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.
34	
35	```js
36	export const meta = {
37	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
38	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
39	};
40	
41	export const schema = {
42	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
43	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
44	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
45	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
46	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
47	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
48	};
49	
50	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
51	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
52	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
53	    { clamp: true });
54	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
55	  return svg(ctx, `
56	    <g opacity="${fade}">
57	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
58	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
59	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
60	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
61	    </g>`);
62	}
63	```
64	
65	| Export | Required | What it is |
66	| --- | --- | --- |
67	| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
68	| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
69	| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |
70	
71	`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.
72	
73	`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.
74	
75	The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
76	
77	## `meta`
78	
79	Every key is optional.
80	
81	| Key | What it does |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
84	| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
85	| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
86	| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
87	| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |
88	
89	A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.
90	
91	## `ctx`
92	
93	`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.
94	
95	| Key | What it is |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
98	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
99	| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
100	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
101	| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
102	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |
103	
104	## Resolution-independent drawing
105	
106	Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.
107	
108	A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:
109	
110	```js
111	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
112	```
113	
114	On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
115	
116	## The schema
117	
118	The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.
119	
120	| Rule | Limit |
121	| --- | --- |
122	| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
123	| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
124	| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
125	| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |
126	
127	`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
128	
129	A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.
130	
131	## Prop types
132	
133	| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
134	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
135	| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
136	| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
137	| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
138	| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
139	| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
140	| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |
141	
142	- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
143	- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
144	- **`asset`.** `render` gets `null` for both `null` and `""`, so test for it before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.
145	
146	## Tolerant props
147	
148	`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.
149	
150	A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:
151	
152	```text
153	props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
154	```
155	
156	A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for how those stale rows show in the inspector.
157	
158	## The SVG the engine draws
159	
160	Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg. It draws text with the graphics' fonts, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.
161	
162	An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
163	
164	These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:
165	
166	| Warning | What to do |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
169	| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
170	| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
171	| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |
172	
173	A size mismatch warns too, but the picture still draws: `the SVG is 100×100 but the graphic is 1920×1080`. Using `svg(ctx, body)` for the root element avoids it.
174	
175	SVG that can't be read at all is an error, and starts `the SVG did not parse:`.
176	
177	## The sandbox
178	
179	A graphic can only use its `frame`, `props`, `ctx`, fonts and pictures, so the same frame with the same properties always draws the same pixels. These stop with an error:
180	
181	| In your module | The error |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| `Math.random()` | `Math.random is not available; use random(seed)` |
184	| `import x from "x"` | `imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global` |
185	| `new Function("…")` | `Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code` |
186	| `eval("…")` | `ReferenceError: eval is not defined` |
187	
188	There's also no `fetch`, no file access, no clock, no `performance`, no `WebAssembly` and no `Intl`. For numbers with thousands separators, use `formatNumber`.
189	
190	`Date` is frozen. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 1 January 2000 at 00:00 UTC. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
191	
192	## Modern JavaScript
193	
194	Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`, `**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll` and `findLast`.
195	
196	## The time budget
197	
198	A runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging Frame Job, because every call has a deadline.
199	
200	| Where | Budget |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| Each frame in the preview | 250 ms |
203	| Each frame in an export | 2 s |
204	| The module's top level, when it compiles | 250 ms |
205	
206	Over the budget, the answer is an error such as:
207	
208	```text
209	over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError: interrupted)
210	```
211	
212	When that error gives a line and column, they're where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
213	
214	## Limits
215	
216	Each module runs in an engine of its own, with these limits:
217	
218	| Limit | Amount | Past it |
219	| --- | --- | --- |
220	| Heap | 64 MB | An error with a line and column |
221	| Stack | 1 MB | An error with a line and column |
222	| A graphic's side | 8192 pixels | Frame Job won't draw it |
223	| The SVG `render` returns | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) | `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most 8388608 bytes` |
224	
225	`render` must return a string that starts with `<svg`. Anything else is an error:
226	
227	| What happened | The error |
228	| --- | --- |
229	| No `return` | ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?`` |
230	| A string that isn't SVG | `render returned a string that does not start with <svg at frame 12: …` |
231	| No `render` exported | ``the module exports no `render` function`` |
232	
233	A frame that fails draws a red error card on the clip. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for where errors and warnings show.

1	// app/Sources/AgentServer+GraphicRender.swift — `render_graphic` (road map
2	// 10 §5h, G4b): a module drawn WITHOUT a clip, as a contact sheet of up to
3	// sixteen frames with each frame number printed under its cell, or as one
4	// frame's SVG text.
5	//
6	// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), `render_frame`'s
7	// posture: sixteen 4K frames are seconds of work, and freezing the UI for them
8	// is not acceptable. Every document touch is inside one `onMain` — the
9	// target, the module as the registry compiled it, the canvas — and the draw
10	// after it is the engine's, which is any-thread (`GraphicModule.svg`,
11	// `GraphicLibrary.rasterize`). The module is held for the whole call, and it
12	// holds its library strongly, so a rescan mid-call swaps the registry's set
13	// and not this one.
14	//
15	// **The ctx is the clip's, with no clip** (`recipe_graphic.rs`'s keys
16	// exactly): the canvas's fps, `durationInFrames` from `meta` (else 5 s at
17	// that rate, ceiled), the module's size from the caller, else `meta`, else
18	// the canvas — `add_graphic_clip`'s defaults — and the project's canvas.
19	// A frame that throws or will not rasterize is its error card on the sheet
20	// and a sentence in the reply; a warning is a sentence too.
21	//
22	// **`format` is read and checked first** (spec §11 G-19): with svg a
23	// non-null `path`, `background` or `max_width` — the png sheet's — is refused
24	// by name, before the multi-frame refusal, since svg answers text and writes
25	// no file. A frame at or past `durationInFrames` is DRAWN, not refused, with
26	// `progress` clamped at 1: a clip longer than its length draws those frames
27	// too (G-9, G-19 (b)). A png sheet past `GraphicContactSheet.maxCellPixels`
28	// of frames is refused once the size is known, before any frame is drawn
29	// or any file written (G-20 (d)).
30	
31	import Foundation
32	
33	extension AgentServer {
34	
35	    /// `render_graphic` — UI path: none — the preview well is a person's
36	    /// picture; §5j builds no strip.
37	    func renderGraphic(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
38	        let name = try requiredString(a, "name")
39	        let frames = try graphicFrames(a)
40	        let propsJSON = try graphicPropsJSON(a)
41	        let requestedWidth = try graphicSide(a, "width")
42	        let requestedHeight = try graphicSide(a, "height")
43	        let format = try stringArg(a, "format") ?? "png"
44	        guard format == "png" || format == "svg" else {
45	            throw ToolError(message: "format must be png or svg (got \"\(format)\").")
46	        }
47	        if format == "svg" {
48	            let sheetOnly = ["path", "background", "max_width"].filter {
49	                a[$0].map { !($0 is NSNull) } ?? false
50	            }
51	            if !sheetOnly.isEmpty {
52	                throw ToolError(
53	                    message: "format svg takes no path, background or max_width — those are the "
54	                        + "png contact sheet's; svg answers one frame's SVG text in the reply and "
55	                        + "writes no file (got \(sheetOnly.joined(separator: ", "))).")
56	            }
57	            if frames.count > 1 {
58	                throw ToolError(
59	                    message: "format svg answers ONE frame's SVG, and frames names "
60	                        + "\(frames.count); ask for one frame, or for a png contact sheet.")
61	            }
62	        }
63	        let maxWidth = try intArg(a, "max_width") ?? GraphicContactSheet.maxWidthDefault
64	        let widths = GraphicContactSheet.maxWidthMin...GraphicContactSheet.maxSide
65	        guard widths.contains(maxWidth) else {
66	            throw ToolError(
67	                message: "max_width must be \(widths.lowerBound)…\(widths.upperBound) px "
68	                    + "(got \(maxWidth)).")
69	        }
70	        let backgroundName = try stringArg(a, "background") ?? "transparent"
71	        guard let background = GraphicSheetBackground(backgroundName) else {
72	            throw ToolError(
73	                message: "background must be \(GraphicSheetBackground.accepted) "
74	                    + "(got \"\(backgroundName)\").")
75	        }
76	        let url = format == "png" ? try graphicSheetDestination(a, name: name) : nil
77	
78	        let context = try onMain {
79	            () throws -> (module: GraphicModule, width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps,
80	                canvas: CanvasSnapshot, frames: Int) in
81	            let document = try self.target(a)
82	            let compiled = try self.compiledModule(named: name, document)
83	            let canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
84	            let tick = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
85	            let width = try requestedWidth.map(Int.init)
86	                ?? Self.metaWhole(compiled.meta, "width", name, in: Self.sides) ?? canvas.width
87	            let height = try requestedHeight.map(Int.init)
88	                ?? Self.metaWhole(compiled.meta, "height", name, in: Self.sides) ?? canvas.height
89	            let length = try Self.metaWhole(
90	                compiled.meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(tick))
91	                ?? Int((5 * canvas.fps.double).rounded(.up))
92	            return (compiled.module, width, height, canvas.fps, canvas, length)
93	        }
94	        let pixels = frames.count * context.width * context.height
95	        if format == "png", pixels > GraphicContactSheet.maxCellPixels {
96	            throw ToolError(
97	                message: "A contact sheet draws at most \(GraphicContactSheet.maxCellPixels) px of "
98	                    + "frames; \(frames.count) frame(s) of \(context.width)×\(context.height) are "
99	                    + "\(pixels) px — ask for fewer frames or a smaller width and height.")
100	        }
101	
102	        var reports: [GraphicReport] = []
103	        var cells: [GraphicSheetCell] = []
104	        for frame in frames {
105	            let ctx = Self.graphicContext(
106	                frame: frame, fps: context.fps, length: context.frames, width: context.width,
107	                height: context.height, canvas: context.canvas)
108	            let drawn: (svg: String, warnings: [GraphicDiagnostic])
109	            do {
110	                drawn = try context.module.svg(
111	                    frame: frame, propsJSON: propsJSON, ctxJSON: Self.jsonText(ctx),
112	                    budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
113	            } catch {
114	                let diagnostics = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
115	                if format == "svg" {
116	                    return try svgReply(name, frame, nil, diagnostics, ctx)
117	                }
118	                reports.append(
119	                    GraphicReport(name: name, frame: frame, failed: true, diagnostics: diagnostics))
120	                cells.append(Self.cardCell(name, frame, diagnostics))
121	                continue
122	            }
123	            if format == "svg" {
124	                return try svgReply(name, frame, drawn.svg, drawn.warnings, ctx)
125	            }
126	            if !drawn.warnings.isEmpty {
127	                reports.append(
128	                    GraphicReport(name: name, frame: frame, failed: false, diagnostics: drawn.warnings))
129	            }
130	            do {
131	                let raster = try context.module.library.rasterize(
132	                    drawn.svg, width: context.width, height: context.height)
133	                if !raster.warnings.isEmpty {
134	                    reports.append(GraphicReport(
135	                        name: name, frame: frame, failed: false, diagnostics: raster.warnings))
136	                }
137	                cells.append(GraphicSheetCell(frame: frame, image: raster.cgImage(), cardText: nil))
138	            } catch {
139	                let diagnostics = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
140	                reports.append(
141	                    GraphicReport(name: name, frame: frame, failed: true, diagnostics: diagnostics))
142	                cells.append(Self.cardCell(name, frame, diagnostics))
143	            }
144	        }
145	
146	        let layout = GraphicContactSheet.layout(
147	            count: cells.count, cellWidth: context.width, cellHeight: context.height,
148	            maxWidth: maxWidth)
149	        guard let url = url,
150	            let sheet = GraphicContactSheet.paint(cells, layout: layout, background: background)
151	        else {
152	            throw ToolError(
153	                message: "The contact sheet of \(layout.width)×\(layout.height) px could not be "
154	                    + "painted.")
155	        }
156	        do {
157	            try FrameWriter.write(sheet, as: .png, to: url)
158	        } catch {
159	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
160	        }
161	        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else {
162	            throw ToolError(message: "Wrote \(url.path) but could not read it back.")
163	        }
164	        let listed = frames.map(String.init).joined(separator: ", ")
165	        var text = "Contact sheet of \(frames.count) frame(s) of \"\(name)\" — frames \(listed) — "
166	            + "each \(context.width)×\(context.height) px at scale "
167	            + String(format: "%g", layout.scale)
168	            + " on \(layout.columns)×\(layout.rows), \(layout.width)×\(layout.height) px, "
169	            + "background \(backgroundName)."
170	        for report in reports {
171	            text += " " + Self.graphicSentence(report)
172	        }
173	        text += " Written to \(url.path)."
174	        return try callResult(
175	            content: [
176	                ["type": "image", "data": data.base64EncodedString(), "mimeType": "image/png"],
177	                ["type": "text", "text": text],
178	            ], isError: false)
179	    }

181	    /// `frames` (1…16 whole numbers ≥ 0) or `frame`, never both; `[0]` for
182	    /// neither.
183	    private func graphicFrames(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> [Int] {
184	        let single = try intArg(a, "frame")
185	        let listed = a["frames"].flatMap { $0 is NSNull ? nil : $0 }
186	        if single != nil, listed != nil {
187	            throw ToolError(message: "frame and frames are exclusive — pass one or the other.")
188	        }
189	        if let single = single {
190	            guard single >= 0 else { throw ToolError(message: "frame must be 0 or more: \(single).") }
191	            return [single]
192	        }
193	        guard let listed = listed else { return [0] }
194	        let limit = GraphicContactSheet.maxFrames
195	        guard let list = listed as? [Any], (1...limit).contains(list.count) else {
196	            throw ToolError(message: "frames must be a list of 1 to \(limit) frame numbers.")
197	        }
198	        return try list.enumerated().map { index, raw in
199	            guard let number = raw as? NSNumber, CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID(),
200	                let whole = AgentServer.whole(number), whole >= 0
201	            else {
202	                throw ToolError(
203	                    message: "frames[\(index)] must be a whole frame number of 0 or more "
204	                        + "(got \(AgentServer.describe(raw))).")
205	            }
206	            return whole
207	        }
208	    }

210	    /// `props` as the JSON text the engine takes; `{}` when absent.
211	    private func graphicPropsJSON(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
212	        guard let raw = a["props"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return "{}" }
213	        guard let props = raw as? [String: Any] else {
214	            throw ToolError(message: "props must be an object keyed by the schema's names")
215	        }
216	        return Self.jsonText(props)
217	    }

219	    /// Where the sheet is written: `path` through `destinationURL` as a
220	    /// `.png`, its folder required to exist; else a temporary file.
221	    private func graphicSheetDestination(_ a: [String: Any], name: String) throws -> URL {
222	        guard let path = try stringArg(a, "path") else {
223	            return Self.temporaryOutput("framejob-graphic-\(name)", extension: "png")
224	        }
225	        return try Self.requireFolder(
226	            of: Self.destinationURL(try Self.nonEmptyOutputPath(path), extension: "png"))
227	    }

229	    /// `recipe_graphic.rs`'s ctx for `frame` of a `length`-frame graphic.
230	    static func graphicContext(
231	        frame: Int, fps: Fps, length: Int, width: Int, height: Int, canvas: CanvasSnapshot
232	    ) -> [String: Any] {
233	        let rate = fps.double
234	        let progress = min(max(Double(frame) / Double(max(length - 1, 1)), 0), 1)
235	        return [
236	            "fps": rate, "time": rate > 0 ? Double(frame) / rate : 0,
237	            "durationInFrames": length, "progress": progress,
238	            "width": width, "height": height,
239	            "canvas": ["width": canvas.width, "height": canvas.height],
240	        ]
241	    }
242	
243	    /// The `svg` format's answer: one frame's text, or why there is none.
244	    private func svgReply(
245	        _ name: String, _ frame: Int, _ svg: String?, _ diagnostics: [GraphicDiagnostic],
246	        _ ctx: [String: Any]
247	    ) throws -> String {
248	        try jsonResult([
249	            "name": name, "frame": frame, "ok": svg != nil, "svg": svg ?? NSNull(),
250	            "diagnostics": diagnostics.map(Self.diagnosticJSON), "ctx": ctx,
251	        ])
252	    }

254	    private static func cardCell(
255	        _ name: String, _ frame: Int, _ diagnostics: [GraphicDiagnostic]
256	    ) -> GraphicSheetCell {
257	        GraphicSheetCell(
258	            frame: frame, image: nil,
259	            cardText: LayerRenderers.errorCardText(
260	                name: name, frame: frame, diagnostic: diagnostics.first))

263	    private static func jsonText(_ object: [String: Any]) -> String {
264	        guard let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: object) else { return "{}" }
265	        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
266	    }

2	// 10 §5h, G3b): `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`; and G4a's three
3	// app-state tools, the agent's write/read loop over the package's
4	// `graphics/`: `write_graphic`, `get_graphic` and `graphic_reference`, with
5	// `graphicsSummary`, which `get_project` reports as `graphics`. G4b's three
6	// are next door: `render_graphic` in `AgentServer+GraphicRender.swift`, the
7	// two imports in `AgentServer+GraphicImports.swift`; and issue batch B84's
8	// three — `delete_graphic`, `rename_graphic`, `restore_graphic` — in
9	// `AgentServer+GraphicFiles.swift`.
10	//
11	// **The app fills `schema`, and only the app can** (G-4): the core has no
12	// filesystem, so the schema a `props` patch is checked against is read here
13	// from the module's CURRENT revision — `GraphicRegistry`'s compiled entry for
14	// the document — and sent with the op. The tool does not publish `schema`
15	// (`AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`'s `.filledByTheApp` rows), so the gate
16	// refuses a caller's own as a stranger before a handler runs.
17	//
18	// What this side refuses is what the core cannot know: a module the folder
19	// does not hold, a module that did not compile, and a `meta` value that
20	// cannot be a duration or a side. Every rule about the props themselves is
21	// the core's sentence.

29	    /// (`EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift`).

95	    static let notUndoableNote = "not undoable; keep your own copy if you want the old one back"

97	    /// `write_graphic` — UI path: the file on disk (an external editor);
98	    /// Insert ▸ Graphic…'s sheet, which writes a template or a chosen `.js` through
99	    /// the same `store.write` then places it (`add_graphic_clip`); and

101	    /// `store.write` then repoints with `set_graphic {name}`.
102	    ///
103	    /// Writes `graphics/<name>.js` through the store's one writer, then
104	    /// rescans at once, so the registry has compiled THAT text before the
105	    /// reply is built: a failed compile is an answer (`ok` false with its
106	    /// diagnostics), not an error. Not undoable and never dirty (G-3); the
107	    /// text it replaced is kept by that rescan's pass, and `kept` lists the
108	    /// module's kept revisions, newest first (G-29).
109	    func writeGraphic(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
110	        let document = try target(a)
111	        let name = try requiredString(a, "name")
112	        let source = try requiredString(a, "source")
113	        let store = try graphicStore(document)
114	        do {
115	            try store.write(name: name, source: source)
116	        } catch let error as ReelCoreError {
117	            throw ToolError(message: error.message)
118	        } catch {
119	            throw ToolError(
120	                message: "graphics/\(name).js could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
121	        }
122	        store.rescan()
123	        guard store.module(named: name) != nil else {
124	            throw ToolError(
125	                message: "graphics/\(name).js was written but the folder's scan does not list it "
126	                    + "— graphics/ may not be readable by Frame Job, or was replaced mid-write; "
127	                    + "get_graphic {} shows what the scan sees")
128	        }
129	        var result = moduleReport(named: name, document)
130	        result["name"] = name
131	        result["kept"] = store.kept(named: name).map(\.revision)
132	        result["note"] = Self.keptNote
133	        return try jsonResult(result)

143	    /// name with a kept revision, deleted modules included (G-29 (e)).

190	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else { return [] }
191	        return store.scan.modules.values.sorted { $0.name < $1.name }.map { file in
192	            let ok: Bool
193	            if case .compiled = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(

195	            {
196	                ok = true
197	            } else {
198	                ok = false

224	    /// the scan holds; a compiled module's diagnostics are what its top level
225	    /// warned (G-24 (a)).

227	        let file = document.graphicStore?.module(named: name)
228	        var result: [String: Any] = [
229	            "path": file?.url.path ?? NSNull(),
230	            "revision": file?.revision ?? NSNull(),
231	            "clips": clipsUsing(name, document),
232	        ]
233	        switch GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: document.recipeKey) {
234	        case .compiled(let module, _, let meta, let schema):
235	            result["ok"] = true
236	            result["meta"] = meta
237	            result["schema"] = schema
238	            result["diagnostics"] = module.compileWarnings.map(Self.diagnosticJSON)
239	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _):

241	            result["meta"] = [String: Any]()
242	            result["schema"] = [String: Any]()

268	            "line": d.line ?? NSNull(), "column": d.column ?? NSNull(),
269	            "frame": d.frame ?? NSNull(),

277	    /// A module, its `meta` and its `schema` from its current revision, or
278	    /// the sentence saying the folder does not hold it or it did not compile.

280	        named name: String, _ document: ProjectDocument
281	    ) throws -> (module: GraphicModule, meta: [String: Any], schema: [String: Any]) {
282	        guard document.graphicStore?.module(named: name) != nil,
283	            let entry = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: document.recipeKey)
284	        else { throw ToolError(message: noModuleSentence(name, document)) }
285	        switch entry {
286	        case .compiled(let module, _, let meta, let schema):
287	            return (module, meta, schema)
288	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _):
289	            let first = diagnostics.first
290	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
291	            throw ToolError(
292	                message: "The module \"\(name)\" does not compile: "
293	                    + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic") + line)

305	    /// `width` or `height` as a side, refused by name outside 1…8192.
306	    func graphicSide(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> UInt32? {
307	        guard let value = try intArg(a, key) else { return nil }
308	        guard Self.sides.contains(value) else {
309	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) is not a side of 1–\(GraphicLibrary.maxSide): \(value)")
310	        }

314	    /// `meta[key]` as a whole number in `range`, nil when the module does
315	    /// not declare it, refused by name when it declares something else.
316	    static func metaWhole(
317	        _ meta: [String: Any], _ key: String, _ name: String, in range: ClosedRange<Int>
318	    ) throws -> Int? {
319	        guard let raw = meta[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
320	        let number = (raw as? NSNumber).flatMap {
321	            CFGetTypeID($0) == CFBooleanGetTypeID() ? nil : AgentServer.whole($0)
322	        }
323	        guard let value = number, range.contains(value) else {
324	            throw ToolError(
325	                message: "meta.\(key) of module \"\(name)\" is not a whole number of "
326	                    + "\(range.lowerBound)–\(range.upperBound): \(raw)")

1	// app/Sources/GraphicContactSheet.swift — `render_graphic`'s contact sheet
2	// (road map 10 §5h, G4b): the frames of one module laid out on a grid, each
3	// with its frame number printed in a strip under it. Pure: cells in, one
4	// `CGImage` out; no document, no file, no thread of its own.
5	//
6	// **The scale is over the CELLS alone** (G4b's objection 2): the gaps and
7	// the label strips are drawn at full size and never scaled, so the bound
8	// they are subtracted from is exactly the sheet's size — `width ≤ maxWidth`
9	// and `height ≤ maxSide` hold by construction.
10	//
11	// **At scale 1 a cell is the raster's own bytes**: drawn at its exact pixel
12	// size and an integer origin, so no resampling touches it and a proof can
13	// compare it with `render_frame`'s picture pixel for pixel. A cell whose
14	// frame failed is the error card, through the one painter
15	// (`LayerRenderers.paintErrorCard`).
16	
17	import AppKit
18	import CoreText
19	
20	/// What the sheet is painted on before the cells.
21	enum GraphicSheetBackground {
22	    case transparent, checker, color(CGColor)
23	
24	    static let accepted = "transparent, checker, or a hex colour (#rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa)"
25	
26	    /// `transparent`, `checker`, or `#rgb` / `#rrggbb` / `#rrggbbaa`, in any
27	    /// case; nil for anything else.
28	    init?(_ argument: String) {
29	        let lowered = argument.lowercased()
30	        switch lowered {
31	        case "transparent":
32	            self = .transparent
33	        case "checker":
34	            self = .checker
35	        default:
36	            guard lowered.hasPrefix("#") else { return nil }
37	            let hex = Array(lowered.dropFirst())
38	            guard [3, 6, 8].contains(hex.count), hex.allSatisfy(\.isHexDigit) else { return nil }
39	            let digits = hex.count == 3 ? hex.flatMap { [$0, $0] } : hex
40	            var channels = stride(from: 0, to: digits.count, by: 2).map { at -> CGFloat in
41	                CGFloat(UInt8(String(digits[at...at + 1]), radix: 16) ?? 0) / 255
42	            }
43	            if channels.count == 3 { channels.append(1) }
44	            self = .color(CGColor(
45	                srgbRed: channels[0], green: channels[1], blue: channels[2], alpha: channels[3]))
46	        }
47	    }
48	}
49	
50	/// One cell: the frame it shows and either its picture or its card's text.
51	struct GraphicSheetCell {
52	    let frame: Int
53	    let image: CGImage?
54	    let cardText: String?
55	}
56	
57	enum GraphicContactSheet {
58	    static let gap = 8, labelHeight = 24, maxWidthDefault = 2048, maxWidthMin = 64
59	    static let maxFrames = 16, maxSide = GraphicLibrary.maxSide
60	    /// The most pixels of frames a png sheet draws (spec §11 G-20 (d)):
61	    /// every cell's raster is held until paint. Two 8192² frames, or
62	    /// sixteen 3840×2160.
63	    static let maxCellPixels = 2 * maxSide * maxSide
64	
65	    /// Where every cell goes. Row-major from the top left, no outer margin.
66	    struct Layout {
67	        let columns, rows: Int
68	        let scale: Double
69	        let cellWidth, cellHeight, width, height: Int
70	
71	        /// Cell `index`'s top-left corner, y down.
72	        func origin(of index: Int) -> (x: Int, y: Int) {
73	            let column = index % columns, row = index / columns
74	            return (
75	                column * (cellWidth + GraphicContactSheet.gap),
76	                row * (cellHeight + GraphicContactSheet.labelHeight + GraphicContactSheet.gap))
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    /// `count` cells of `cellWidth`×`cellHeight` on a near-square grid, the
81	    /// cells scaled down (never up) so the sheet is at most `maxWidth` wide
82	    /// and `maxSide` tall.
83	    static func layout(count: Int, cellWidth: Int, cellHeight: Int, maxWidth: Int) -> Layout {
84	        let count = max(count, 1)
85	        var columns = 1
86	        while columns * columns < count { columns += 1 }
87	        let rows = (count + columns - 1) / columns
88	        let byWidth = Double(maxWidth - (columns - 1) * gap) / Double(columns * cellWidth)
89	        let byHeight = Double(maxSide - rows * labelHeight - (rows - 1) * gap)
90	            / Double(rows * cellHeight)
91	        let scale = min(1, byWidth, byHeight)
92	        let drawnWidth = max(1, Int((Double(cellWidth) * scale).rounded(.down)))
93	        let drawnHeight = max(1, Int((Double(cellHeight) * scale).rounded(.down)))
94	        return Layout(
95	            columns: columns, rows: rows, scale: scale,
96	            cellWidth: drawnWidth, cellHeight: drawnHeight,
97	            width: columns * drawnWidth + (columns - 1) * gap,
98	            height: rows * (drawnHeight + labelHeight) + (rows - 1) * gap)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// The sheet: `background`, then each cell at `layout`'s place with its
102	    /// label strip under it. Premultiplied BGRA in sRGB, exactly
103	    /// `layout.width`×`layout.height`.
104	    static func paint(
105	        _ cells: [GraphicSheetCell], layout: Layout, background: GraphicSheetBackground
106	    ) -> CGImage? {
107	        guard let space = CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.sRGB),
108	            let context = CGContext(
109	                data: nil, width: layout.width, height: layout.height, bitsPerComponent: 8,
110	                bytesPerRow: 0, space: space,
111	                bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedFirst.rawValue
112	                    | CGBitmapInfo.byteOrder32Little.rawValue)
113	        else { return nil }
114	        let whole = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: layout.width, height: layout.height)
115	        switch background {
116	        case .transparent:
117	            context.clear(whole)
118	        case .color(let color):
119	            context.setFillColor(color)
120	            context.fill(whole)
121	        case .checker:
122	            paintChecker(context, width: layout.width, height: layout.height)
123	        }
124	        context.interpolationQuality = layout.scale < 1 ? .high : .none
125	        for (index, cell) in cells.enumerated() {
126	            let (x, top) = layout.origin(of: index)
127	            // Core Graphics is y up: the cell's bottom edge, from the top-left place.
128	            let rect = CGRect(
129	                x: x, y: layout.height - top - layout.cellHeight,
130	                width: layout.cellWidth, height: layout.cellHeight)
131	            if let text = cell.cardText {
132	                LayerRenderers.paintErrorCard(text, in: context, bounds: rect)
133	            } else if let image = cell.image {
134	                context.draw(image, in: rect)
135	            }
136	            paintLabel(
137	                cell.frame, in: context,
138	                strip: CGRect(
139	                    x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY - CGFloat(labelHeight), width: rect.width,
140	                    height: CGFloat(labelHeight)))
141	        }
142	        return context.makeImage()
143	    }
144	
145	    /// 16 px squares of (128,128,128) and (192,192,192), from the top left.
146	    static func paintChecker(_ context: CGContext, width: Int, height: Int) {
147	        let side = 16
148	        context.setFillColor(CGColor(srgbRed: 128 / 255, green: 128 / 255, blue: 128 / 255, alpha: 1))
149	        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: width, height: height))
150	        context.setFillColor(CGColor(srgbRed: 192 / 255, green: 192 / 255, blue: 192 / 255, alpha: 1))
151	        for row in 0...(height / side) {
152	            for column in 0...(width / side) where (row + column) % 2 == 1 {
153	                context.fill(CGRect(
154	                    x: column * side, y: height - (row + 1) * side, width: side, height: side))
155	            }
156	        }
157	    }
158	
159	    /// The frame number in white `DS.mono(13)` on an opaque (30,30,30) strip,
160	    /// clipped to the strip.
161	    private static func paintLabel(_ frame: Int, in context: CGContext, strip: CGRect) {
162	        context.saveGState()
163	        defer { context.restoreGState() }
164	        context.clip(to: strip)
165	        context.setFillColor(CGColor(srgbRed: 30 / 255, green: 30 / 255, blue: 30 / 255, alpha: 1))
166	        context.fill(strip)
167	        let attributed = NSAttributedString(
168	            string: String(frame),
169	            attributes: [.font: DS.mono(13), .foregroundColor: NSColor.white])
170	        let line = CTLineCreateWithAttributedString(attributed)
171	        context.setFillColor(CGColor(srgbRed: 1, green: 1, blue: 1, alpha: 1))
172	        context.textMatrix = .identity
173	        context.textPosition = CGPoint(x: strip.minX + 6, y: strip.minY + 7)
174	        CTLineDraw(line, context)
175	    }
176	}

178	extension GraphicRaster {
179	    /// The raster as a `CGImage`: premultiplied BGRA in sRGB, rows `stride`
180	    /// bytes apart — the layout the engine wrote, so nothing is converted.
181	    func cgImage() -> CGImage? {
182	        guard width > 0, height > 0, let space = CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.sRGB),
183	            let provider = CGDataProvider(data: Data(bgra) as CFData)
184	        else { return nil }
185	        return CGImage(
186	            width: width, height: height, bitsPerComponent: 8, bitsPerPixel: 32,
187	            bytesPerRow: stride, space: space,
188	            bitmapInfo: CGBitmapInfo(
189	                rawValue: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedFirst.rawValue
190	                    | CGBitmapInfo.byteOrder32Little.rawValue),
191	            provider: provider, decode: nil, shouldInterpolate: false, intent: .defaultIntent)
192	    }

26	extension AgentServer {
27	
28	    /// `list_graphics` — UI path: Insert ▸ Graphic…'s two lists.

46	    /// What `name` and `from` name in Insert ▸ Graphic…'s lists.
47	    enum BrowserGraphic {
48	        case template(GraphicTemplateLibrary.Entry)
49	        case project(String)
50	    }

52	    /// `name` resolved in the origin `from` names, refused in `insert_graphic`'s sentences:
53	    /// a `from` that is neither origin, a document with no window, a name that origin does
54	    /// not hold. Main.
55	    func browserGraphic(
56	        name: String, from: String, document: ProjectDocument
57	    ) throws -> BrowserGraphic {
58	        guard let origin = GraphicBrowserItem.Origin(rawValue: from) else {

1	// app/Sources/ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift — the two halves of
2	// Insert ▸ Graphic… that both doors share (spec §11 G-16, G-45 (f)): the
3	// sheet's Insert and From File… (`EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift`)
4	// and `insert_graphic` (`AgentServer+GraphicBrowser.swift`).
5	//
6	// `writeGraphicModule` is G-16 (b): a module's text copied into the
7	// package's `graphics/` under a free name, then the folder rescanned so the
8	// registry has compiled THAT text. `rescan()` runs here, from a command,
9	// never from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer (`drain()` is not re-entrant).
10	// The file write is not undoable (G-3).
11	//
12	// `graphicClipMaker` is the clip: `add_graphic_clip` at the module's `meta`
13	// duration and size, with the schema of its current revision (G-4). Where
14	// the clip goes is each caller's: `EditorViewController.generatedClipOps`,
15	// Add Text's rule (G-16 (a)). A module that does not compile places nothing
16	// and throws its first diagnostic (G-45 (f)).
17	
18	import Foundation
19	
20	extension ProjectDocument {
21	    /// The sentence for a document whose graphics store has not started —
22	    /// one with no window.
23	    static let noGraphicsFolderSentence =
24	        "This project has no graphics folder open (its window has not been made)"
25	
26	    /// Writes `url`'s module into `graphics/` under a free name made from
27	    /// its stem (G-16 (b)) and rescans; the name it was written under.
28	    /// Throws, writing nothing, when the file cannot be read or is not
29	    /// UTF-8.
30	    func writeGraphicModule(from url: URL) throws -> String {
31	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
32	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
33	        }
34	        let bytes: Data
35	        do {
36	            bytes = try Data(contentsOf: url)
37	        } catch {
38	            throw ReelCoreError(
39	                message: "\(url.path) could not be read: \(error.localizedDescription)")
40	        }
41	        guard let source = String(data: bytes, encoding: .utf8) else {
42	            throw ReelCoreError(
43	                message: "\(url.path) is not UTF-8 text — a graphic module must be UTF-8 "
44	                    + "JavaScript")
45	        }
46	        let name = store.uniqueModuleName(
47	            GraphicTemplates.moduleName(from: url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent))
48	        try store.write(name: name, source: source)
49	        store.rescan()
50	        return name
51	    }
52	
53	    /// The op that places one clip drawn by `graphics/<name>.js` at a track
54	    /// and a time: its `meta` duration and size, its schema. Throws the
55	    /// module's first diagnostic when it does not compile, the store's
56	    /// sentence when the folder does not hold it, and the `meta` sentence
57	    /// when a duration or side is not a whole number in range.
58	    func graphicClipMaker(named name: String) throws -> (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp {
59	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
60	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
61	        }
62	        guard let entry = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: recipeKey) else {
63	            throw ReelCoreError(message: store.noModuleSentence(name))
64	        }
65	        guard case .compiled(_, _, let meta, let schema) = entry else {
66	            var first: GraphicDiagnostic?
67	            if case .failed(let diagnostics, _) = entry { first = diagnostics.first }
68	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
69	            throw ReelCoreError(
70	                message: "graphics/\(name).js does not compile: "
71	                    + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic") + line)
72	        }
73	        let frame = max(project.snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
74	        let duration: Ticks?
75	        let width: UInt32?
76	        let height: UInt32?
77	        do {
78	            duration = try AgentServer.metaWhole(
79	                meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(frame)
80	            ).map { Ticks($0) * frame }
81	            width = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "width", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
82	                .map(UInt32.init)
83	            height = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "height", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
84	                .map(UInt32.init)
85	        } catch let error as AgentServer.ToolError {
86	            throw ReelCoreError(message: error.message)
87	        }
88	        return { track, at in
89	            .addGraphicClipRaw(
90	                track: track, at: at, duration: duration, name: name, width: width,
91	                height: height, props: nil, schema: schema)
92	        }
93	    }
94	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can

  on-device analysis of the media (road map creator-jobs CJ2a, spec §11
  CJ-20…CJ-29): a cache made on demand in `cache/analysis/<kind>/`, never at
  import, never project state, never read by the plan or the recipe.
  `AnalysisLane` is the process-wide analysis lane, the analysis twin of
  `MediaCacheLane.swift`'s rule: owners want requests (`want` replaces, an
  unwanted job is cancelled, an owner whose `alive()` is false is dropped at
  the next 50 ms poll, `settled` runs on main), a `.utility` picture queue
  of `pictureWidth` (1, CJ-S3) and a serial sound queue, never the
  cooperative pool and never `MediaCacheLane`; a job takes no `CachePass`
  and writes only through `AnalysisStore.publish` or `publishFile` — a lock
  per (cache, kind, media) inside `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`,
  re-reading and merging what is on disk — so an import pass and a job never
  cancel or wait on each other, and nothing in a publish waits on main. A
  stamp is compared field by field (`AnalysisStamp.matches`).
  `AnalysisFrames` reads direct (turned upright) or converted through
  `MediaImporter.oneClip` and step 0 when a `ThumbnailInput` exists, its
  pre-roll two DECODED frames.
  The `masks` kind (road map creator-jobs CO1, spec §11 CO-10…CO-14):
  `AnalysisMasks` makes a fresh person `.balanced` request (revision 1) per
  frame, pinned to the GPU, and refuses one that reads back another device.
  It also sets the found flag, reads runs from a pack, and publishes every
  30 s and at a range's end, mid-range only through the last analysed frame
  done. `MaskPack` is `masks.pack`, with LZFSE masks in append order, the
  frame and mask tables and a 40-byte `FJMP` footer holding the size Vision
  answered. It has an append-merge writer (on-disk slots never move, on disk
  wins at an equal pts) and a mapped reader. A kind that writes its own
  `.partial` publishes through `AnalysisStore.publishFile`; the marker keeps
  the on-disk coverage only when the write merged, and a lookup hits only
  when its first payload file is on disk. `AnalysisFrames+InputPass` is
  CO-7's third arm: `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` and step 0's `InputPass` to
  SDR in a per-read `.shared` target, every frame's own time kept, for
  `masks` on a converting media (`Source.arm`). `AnalysisClipTimes` is a
  clip's played window (a pure move, CO1's toll), and
  `AgentServer+AnalysisMasks` holds the answer's `mask_size`, `frames`,
  `subject_found` and `runs`, never pixels.
  A picture's masks (road map creator-jobs CO10b, spec §11 CO-105):
  `AnalysisMasks+Image` is `runImage`, one mask per image media and subject
  kind — the `masks` kind's person request for `person`, the `foreground`
  kind's `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (revision 1, pinned to the
  GPU, refused on another device) for `foreground` — on the picture as
  `LayerRenderers.image` decodes it, one frame `(0, 0, 0)` published covering
  `0...0`; `analysisInput` reads a non-video direct; `get_media_analysis`
  lists and accepts `AnalysisKind.mediaAnalysisKinds`, every kind but
  `foreground`.
  The `faces` kind (road map creator-jobs CJ3, spec §11 CJ-30…CJ-35):
  `AnalysisFaces` reads at long side 720 through the standard arms
  (direct, or converted for a converting media) and, per analysed frame,
  makes a FRESH `VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` and a fresh
  `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest` (revision 3, `.constellation76Points`),
  each on a fresh handler and pinned to the Neural Engine; a job refuses a
  request that reads back another device. `AnalysisVision` is the device
  enum and `pin` both Vision kinds use (a pure move out of
  `AnalysisMasks`). Its grid is a sample grid, 10 a second
  (`AnalysisKind.grid(of:)`, `AnalysisGrid(samplesPerSecond:duration:)`):
  sample k takes the first kept frame in `[ticks(k), ticks(k) + one
  interval)`, else pts −1; faces are ordered by box centre x then y, with
  no identity. `AnalysisFaces+Samples` is `samples.bin` (`FJFS`): its codec
  and the publish's decode-and-merge write (an undecodable file is written
  fresh). `AgentServer+AnalysisFaces` holds the answer's rows, every float
  rounded to 4 decimals and written as an `NSDecimalNumber` read in
  `en_US_POSIX` (`JSONSerialization` prints a `Double` to 17 significant
  figures), and the cap's refusal.
  The `subjects` kind (road map creator-jobs VR1, spec §11 VR-10…VR-16):
  `AnalysisSubjects` reads as `faces` does and, per analysed frame, makes a
  FRESH `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` (revision 2, `upperBodyOnly` true,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
